basis.governing_question: Should Quinta Azul enter the Spanish retail market and, if so, how?

phases.name: Research
phases.objective_one_line: Assess the size, competition and buyer needs of the Spanish retail market and Quinta Azul's capability to win there.

gate.label: Findings sign-off
gate.decision: Against the agreed tests, is Spain attractive enough to justify designing entry options?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Compare entry options for Spain, build the business case and draft the entry roadmap for the go or no-go.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the Spain go or no-go decision and, if go, the entry plan?

workstreams.name: Spanish market and channels
workstreams.answers: How large and attractive is the Spanish retail market for Quinta Azul's olive oil, and which channels reach it?
activities: Size Spanish retail demand and growth from market data
Assess channel listing terms, margins and shelf access
Review regulation for selling olive oil in Spain

workstreams.name: Competitor landscape
workstreams.answers: Who competes for Spanish retail shelf space in olive oil, and how do they position their products?
activities: Profile competing olive-oil brands on Spanish shelves
Compare ranges, prices and positioning from store visits
Write up competitor profiles for the steering workshop

workstreams.name: Buyer and shopper needs
workstreams.answers: What do Spanish retail buyers and shoppers need from an olive-oil supplier?
activities: Interview retail buyers on listing criteria and needs
Sample shopper segments by survey or in-store interviews
Write up buyer and shopper findings by channel

workstreams.name: Capability to win in Spain
workstreams.answers: Does Quinta Azul have the assets and capabilities to win in Spanish retail?
activities: Interview staff who run Quinta Azul's operations
Review operational data on capacity and cost to serve
Assess gaps between Quinta Azul's assets and buyer needs

workstreams.name: Entry option business case
workstreams.answers: Which entry options exist for Spain, and does the business case support a go or no-go?
activities: Compare entry options for Spain on agreed criteria
Build the business case from the Research findings
Test cost and margin assumptions against operational data

workstreams.name: Entry plan and roadmap
workstreams.answers: If the answer is go, what entry plan and roadmap should Quinta Azul follow?
activities: Sequence the steps of an entry plan for Spain
Draft the entry roadmap for the chosen option
Review the draft plan with the CEO and Commercial Director

deliverables.name: Spanish retail market and channel assessment
Competitor profiles for Spanish olive-oil retail
Buyer interview findings on listing criteria
Buyer and shopper needs by channel
Gap assessment of Quinta Azul's assets for Spain
Findings pack for the Spain attractiveness decision
Entry options for Spain compared on agreed criteria
Business case for the Spain go or no-go decision
Entry plan and roadmap for Spain

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Launch work and set the success tests
events.decision: Which Quinta Azul data and Spanish buyer contacts will the team get access to?
agenda: Present the phases, gates and what each phase delivers
Discuss access to Quinta Azul data and Spanish buyers
Align on measurable definitions of 'attractive enough' and 'go'

events.label: Workshop: first findings
events.purpose: Review early market and buyer evidence
events.decision: Which buyer listing criteria should the gap assessment of Quinta Azul's assets test?
agenda: Present market, channel and competitor findings
Review buyer interview findings on listing criteria
Decide the criteria for the capability gap assessment

events.label: Findings sign-off
events.purpose: Decide whether Spain justifies entry design
events.decision: Against the agreed tests, is Spain attractive enough to justify designing entry options?
agenda: Present the findings pack for the attractiveness decision
Review buyer and shopper needs and the capability gaps
Decide whether Spain meets the agreed attractiveness tests

events.label: Check-in: business case
events.purpose: Review entry options and business case
events.decision: Which entry option should the entry plan and roadmap detail?
agenda: Present entry options compared on agreed criteria
Review the business case for the go or no-go decision
Decide which option the roadmap details

events.label: Final readout
events.purpose: Approve the go or no-go and entry plan
events.decision: Approve the Spain go or no-go decision and, if go, the entry plan?
agenda: Present the entry plan and roadmap for Spain
Review the business case against the agreed 'go' test
Decide whether to approve the go or no-go and entry plan

architect_notes: Engagement length is not given, so the 11 to 15 weeks are an estimate from the sizing; confirm length and any deadline before quoting.
Confirm the assumed counts behind Research: 3 retail channels, 6 buyer interviews and 2 shopper segments; they size its 8 to 10 weeks.
Design is sized for a go outcome; a no-go would drop the entry roadmap and shorten the phase.

sub_questions.question: How large and attractive is the Spanish retail market for Quinta Azul's olive oil?
Who competes there, and what do Spanish retail buyers and shoppers need?
Does Quinta Azul have the assets and capabilities to win in Spain?
Which entry options exist for Spain, and does the business case support a go or no-go?
If the answer is go, what entry plan and roadmap should Quinta Azul follow?

phases.name: Research

work.unit: Market assessed in full (demand, channels, competitors, regulation, buyer interviews)
Retail channel assessed (listing terms, margins, shelf access)
Retail buyer interview scheduled, held and written up
Shopper segment sampled (survey or in-store interviews)

phases.why: Market first, then 3 channels at once, 6 buyer interviews three at a time, 2 shopper segments; fieldwork puts the maximum 2 weeks over typical.

phases.name: Design

work.unit: Entry option and business case for one market
Entry sequence and roadmap across markets

phases.why: The entry option and business case for Spain come first, then the entry roadmap, one after the other.

sizing.levers: Assessing only the retail channels the CEO and Commercial Director prioritize, and starting the roadmap alongside the business case, would shorten the engagement most.
